questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Continuous Delivery”?
options: Continuous Delivery helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Continuous Delivery means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Continuous Delivery removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Continuous Delivery should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Continuous Delivery helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Continuous Delivery is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Automated deployment” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Automated deployment” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Automated deployment” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Automated deployment” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Automated deployment” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Automated deployment” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Automated deployment” under Continuous Delivery. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Continuous Delivery”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
